text:
maya: Heads-up: saw a regression in p99 tail when we bumped prefetch window and enabled soft token budgets for streaming. Baseline before change: p99 ~ 280ms; after: ~420ms on same load. Noticed more partial-decode stalls and occasional KV cache misses during streams.

carlos: Interesting — are the KV misses correlated with longer seqs or many concurrent short chats?

maya: Mostly short chats (avg 24 tokens). Concurrency up ~20%, but per-request token counts are small. KV metrics show spikes in eviction hits around the same timestamp as the spikes.

eli: Can you paste the batcher config you toggled?

maya: Sure, config snippet we rolled to canary:```yaml
batcher:
  prefetch_window_ms: 35
  max_batch_tokens: 480
  token_budget_target: 10
  token_budget_headroom: 2
  partial_decode_policy: early-priority
  queue_policy: weighted-fair
```

sophie: Nice, that prefetch_window is bigger than our usual 16ms. My suspicion: larger window increases chance of mixing shorter requests with longer ones, which hurts partial-decode scheduling and delays streaming flushes. Also KV cache TTL jitter + heavier batching might evict keys before they are used.

carlos: Agree. Two hypotheses: (1) batching mixes short+long and kernel selection picks a heavier attention kernel for mixed sequences causing decode stalls, (2) token_budget_target=10 is too low when prefetch groups more tokens per batch, so partial-decode threads wait for budget refill.

eli: I profiled a canary run — attaching flame summary link from infra-bot: <https://perf.redwood/trace/1801234> (infra-bot uploaded). Top findings: a) scheduling waits in decode queue increased 45% b) kernel selection cost jumps when batch has >1 long seq c) KV lookup latency 12ms spikes coincident with eviction churn.

infra-bot: perf artifacts: upload complete — /artifacts/1801234/batch-flame.html, /artifacts/1801234/kv-evict.log

maya: Repro recipe is small: run chats workload @1.2x baseline QPS with prefetch=35ms and token_budget_target=10. Quick A/B showed p50 stable, p95 up ~10ms, p99 up ~140ms.

carlos: Quick mitigation options: lower prefetch_window_ms to 12-16ms, or switch queue_policy to "size-aware" that avoids mixing >1 long seq per batch. Also consider raising token_budget_target to 16 to give partial-decode threads more headroom.

eli: Another angle: add a kernel-routing hint when batch contains mixed lengths so we pick the low-latency kernel for majority-of-requests. Could be a small change in kernel selector: if short_frac>0.7 -> pick short-optimized kernel even if a few long sequences present.

maya: I like the size-aware queue policy + token budget bump for short term. We should measure effect on cost though.

sophie: Can we try a two-step canary: A) prefetch 16ms + token_budget_target 16, B) prefetch 35ms + queue_policy size-aware + token_budget 16. Run each for 30m. I'll schedule the experiments.

carlos: I'll push a small selector change behind a flag to add short_frac heuristic. Patch:```diff
+ if batch.short_frac >= 0.7:
+   kernel_hint = "short_fast"
+ else:
+   kernel_hint = default_selector(batch)
```

eli: I'll analyze cost delta offline. If token_budget up -> more peak GPU cycles but should reduce tail latency significantly.

maya: Thanks — sophie, once experiments return can you drop the flame for both and tag me? I'll also run a KV eviction simulation to see if TTL tuning helps.

sophie: Will do. Kicking off A now. ETA 40m.

carlos: Small note: if we keep prefetch high we might need to increase KV cache size or reduce eviction aggressiveness to avoid churn.

maya: Yup. I'll draft a quick runbook with knobs we toggled and expected perf signals.

eli: One more: partial-decode prioritization should prefer requests that have active streaming connections; maybe deprioritize batch completion heuristics that wait for ambiguous tokens.

maya: Good call. We'll iterate. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
